title: PARIVARTAN Scheme gains momentum: 1,300+ beneficiaries registered, 42 Banks/NBFCs and 15 auto OEMs onboarded across Delhi-NCR
body_text:
The Union Cabinet, on 3 rd June 2026, approved the PARIVARTAN (Programme for Accelerated Renewal and Incentivization of Vehicle Assets for Reducing Transport Air Pollution and Network Emissions) Scheme, to replace over 2 lakh trucks and buses conforming to Bharat Stage (BS)-IV or prior emission norms, registered in the National Capital Territory of Delhi and the NCR districts of Haryana, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, with BS-VI or stricter norm compliant or electric vehicles. The Scheme is being funded through the National Capital Region Planning Board (NCRPB) under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) and is being implemented by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH).
The Scheme has a total financial outlay of ₹9,585 crore, including ₹5,041 crore in budgetary support from the Central Government. Eligible beneficiaries purchasing new BS-VI or stricter norm compliant diesel or CNG vehicles, or electric vehicles, are entitled to a package of incentives comprising:
5% interest savings on eligible vehicle loans for 5 years; 100% Road Tax Waiver for a period of 10 years and a full waiver on registration fees (the States of Delhi, Haryana, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh have already issued notifications in this regard); at least 8% discount on ex-showroom price from participating Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs); and monthly fuel vouchers ranging from ₹1,200 to ₹4,800, depending on vehicle category, for a period of five years for buyers of BS-VI diesel or CNG vehicles, or a one-time incentive ranging from ₹64,000 to ₹2.56 lakh for buyers of electric vehicles.
The Scheme was launched on 14 th July 2026 . As on 27 th Aug 2026, 1,300+ beneficiaries have registered on the PARIVARTAN Portal. To extend financing support, 42 banks and non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) have been onboarded to provide interest subvention on vehicle loans. On the industry side, Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) have been signed with 15 auto OEMs to extend the discount to eligible beneficiaries.
A multi-pronged awareness campaign is being undertaken to reach eligible vehicle owners across Delhi-NCR regarding the benefits and registration process under the Scheme. The campaign spans print, electronic and digital media, and outdoor publicity at fuel stations, transport nagars, toll plazas and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across Delhi-NCR, with the aim of driving wider beneficiary registration and participation under the Scheme.
Sh. Mahendra Singh becomes the first vehicle owner to purchase a new vehicle under the PARIVARTAN Scheme, in Alwar, Rajasthan on 19 th August 2026.
***
GDH/DS/HJ

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways reported progress on the PARIVARTAN Scheme, approved by the Union Cabinet on 3 June 2026 to replace over 2 lakh BS-IV or older trucks and buses in Delhi-NCR with BS-VI/electric vehicles. As of 27 August 2026, over 1,300 beneficiaries have registered on the scheme's portal, with 42 banks/NBFCs onboarded for loan interest subvention and 15 auto OEMs signing MoUs to offer purchase discounts. The scheme, launched on 14 July 2026, has a total outlay of ₹9,585 crore (₹5,041 crore central budgetary support) and offers interest savings, road tax and registration fee waivers, OEM discounts, and fuel vouchers or one-time EV incentives.
enrichment.context:
PARIVARTAN is a targeted vehicle-fleet renewal scheme aimed at tackling Delhi-NCR's chronic air pollution crisis, which is significantly worsened by old, high-emission commercial vehicles still plying despite BS-VI norms being mandatory for new vehicles since 2020. It is funded through the National Capital Region Planning Board (NCRPB) under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs but implemented by MoRTH, reflecting an inter-ministerial approach to regional air quality management alongside bodies like the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) in NCR. The scheme's incentive structure—combining interest subvention, tax waivers, OEM discounts, and fuel/EV vouchers—mirrors the design logic of the earlier Vehicle Scrappage Policy (2021) but is more comprehensive in its financial incentives and specifically geographically targeted to the NCR airshed.

This release is essentially a progress/status update rather than a new policy announcement, but it is useful for aspirants to understand the scheme's architecture, funding split, and implementation ecosystem (states' notifications, bank/OEM participation) as a live example of cooperative federalism and multi-agency coordination in environmental governance.

prelims_questions.question: The PARIVARTAN Scheme, aimed at replacing old emission-norm vehicles in Delhi-NCR, is funded through which of the following?
options: National Capital Region Planning Board (NCRPB) under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, PARIVARTAN is funded through the NCRPB under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, while it is implemented by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following incentives is NOT offered under the PARIVARTAN Scheme for eligible vehicle buyers?
options: 5% interest savings on vehicle loans for 5 years
Direct cash subsidy equal to full vehicle cost
At least 8% discount on ex-showroom price from participating OEMs
prelims_questions.explanation: The scheme offers interest savings, tax/registration waivers, OEM discounts, and fuel vouchers/EV incentives, but does not provide a subsidy covering the full vehicle cost.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of vehicle fleet renewal schemes like PARIVARTAN in addressing air pollution in the National Capital Region. What structural challenges could limit their effectiveness?

Examine the role of inter-ministerial and inter-state coordination in the design and implementation of schemes targeting region-specific environmental problems, with reference to the PARIVARTAN Scheme.
mains_questions.gs_paper: GS Paper 2 - Government Policies and Interventions

study_notes.reason: The release gives a testable factual core (scheme name, funding-implementation split, incentive structure, financial outlay) alongside genuine analytical material on inter-ministerial cooperative federalism and vehicle-fleet renewal as an air-pollution governance tool, making it useful both for objective recall and for building policy-analysis answers.

prelims.point: PARIVARTAN Scheme (approved 3 June 2026) aims to replace 2 lakh+ BS-IV or older trucks/buses registered in NCT Delhi and NCR districts of Haryana, Rajasthan and UP with BS-VI/EV vehicles.
prelims.why_important: Full form, target vehicle category, and geographic scope (NCR districts of three states) are classic fact-based UPSC testing points.

prelims.point: PARIVARTAN incentive package: 5% interest subvention on vehicle loans for 5 years, 100% road tax waiver for 10 years, registration fee waiver, minimum 8% OEM discount, monthly fuel vouchers (₹1,200-₹4,800) or one-time EV incentive (₹64,000-₹2.56 lakh).
prelims.why_important: UPSC often frames statement-based questions on specific scheme incentive components and their eligibility conditions.

prelims.point: BS-VI emission norms have been mandatory for new vehicles in India since 2020; PARIVARTAN targets legacy BS-IV or older vehicles still in use.
prelims.why_important: Distinguishing BS-IV from BS-VI and knowing the 2020 mandate date is a recurring environment-policy fact base.

prelims.point: Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) is the statutory body overseeing air quality management in the National Capital Region.
prelims.why_important: CAQM is a frequently referenced institution in NCR pollution governance questions, useful to link with schemes like PARIVARTAN.

mains.point: Persistence of high-emission legacy commercial vehicles despite mandatory BS-VI norms since 2020 is a key driver of Delhi-NCR's chronic air pollution, justifying a targeted fleet-renewal intervention.
mains.analytical_use: Useful for answers analysing causes of NCR air pollution and evaluating regulatory versus incentive-based approaches to phasing out non-compliant vehicles.

mains.point: PARIVARTAN's incentive architecture (interest subvention, tax waivers, OEM discounts, fuel/EV vouchers) builds on and expands the design logic of the 2021 Vehicle Scrappage Policy, but is geographically targeted to the NCR airshed.
mains.analytical_use: Can be used to compare/contrast successive vehicle-renewal policy designs and assess whether targeted regional schemes are more effective than nationwide ones.

mains.point: Only 1,300+ beneficiaries have registered against a target of replacing over 2 lakh vehicles, indicating a significant early implementation gap despite awareness campaigns.
mains.analytical_use: Supports answers on why welfare/environmental schemes often show slow uptake and what factors (awareness, financing, affordability) affect beneficiary participation.

both.concept: PARIVARTAN is funded through the NCRPB under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs but implemented by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, with state governments issuing enabling notifications.
both.prelims_angle: UPSC could test which body funds versus which implements the scheme, and the role of NCRPB.
both.mains_angle: Illustrates a multi-agency, cooperative-federalism model for regional environmental governance, relevant to discussing coordination challenges between central ministries and state governments in NCR pollution control.
